subject: Follow-up: data geography, failover profile, and logging requirements
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sam Heath <sam.heath@medcloud.com>, Ava Liao <ava.liao@medcloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: data geography, failover profile, and logging requirements

Hi Sam / Ava —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation. Per our run-through I wanted to capture the specific asks and proposed next steps so we can move toward a scoped proposal that matches MedCloud's residency and privacy constraints. TL;DR: Redwood can offer region pinning with a warm DR option and configurable log retention; a few items need engineering sign-off (outlined below).

Quick recap of requirements you mentioned on the call:
- PII and patient-linked data must remain in EU (primary processing and storage).
- Cross-region failover is allowed but only as a DR measure; active replication to non-EU regions must be limited and logged.
- Audit logs for access and admin actions needed (90 days preferred; longer archive on request).
- Retention lifecycle: staging data 30 days, production inference artifacts 7 years or per customer policy (TBD).
- Encryption: in transit and at rest required; HSM/KMS integration for key separation desired.

What I can commit to now:
- Region pinning: we can pin customers to an EU region (eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 options) and disable automatic cross-region replication in normal operation.
- Failover: we support a warm-standby DR model (standby cluster in US region) that will only accept traffic after an explicit failover action; we can document the RTO/RPO tradeoffs.
- Logging: configurable retention windows per account; default 90 days for high-volume audit logs and the option to push long-term archives to your S3/GCS with lifecycle rules.
- Encryption: we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private/Dedicated deployments; hosted customers can use our multi-tenant KMS or integrate via an external key broker (we'll map options).

Unknowns / items for Engineering security to validate:
1) KV-cache residency: some models keep transient KV cache in GPU memory; we need to confirm whether any system-level call traces or ephemeral state would be written to non-EU durable stores during failover.
2) Backup snapshot cadence and cross-region snapshot transfer (we will propose weekly snapshot + encrypted transfer for DR; confirm acceptable cadence).
3) Detailed RBAC / field-level audit logs for SRE/admin actions (sample log format to follow).

Attachments: region-pin-matrix.xlsx (matrix of options and tradeoffs).

Next steps / asks:
- Sam: can you confirm the hard requirement for archival retention (is 7 years mandatory or negotiable per dataset)?
- MedCloud: please share any contractual language for data transfer restrictions you expect to see (we can map to our standard clauses).
- Redwood: I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical follow-up with Monica (engineering) to walk the team through the warm-standby configuration and KV/cache behavior.

If this looks right I’ll send an updated MAP and a short config snippet that shows region-pinning toggles.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com | +1 415-555-0193
[Attachment: region-pin-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
From: Sam Heath <sam.heath@medcloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data geography, failover profile, and logging requirements

Thanks Olga — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side after syncing with legal and infra: 

- Archival retention: for patient records related to billing and compliance we have a 7-year floor; for conversational PII (non-billing) our legal team would accept 3 years if we can guarantee no cross-border replication in steady-state.
- Failover behavior: our infra team prefers an automated failover with manual approval window (we want a 15–30 minute human confirmation before promoting DR to primary). Is that supported?
- Logs: 90 days sounds fine for admin/audit logs. For raw model telemetry (token-level logs) we need stricter controls — ideally token telemetry not be stored longer than 30 days and be available for on-prem archival if necessary.

Two asks: 1) sample region-pin config (yaml or JSON) so our infra folks can review; 2) an explicit statement on whether Redwood ever performs cross-region replication of primary data during normal ops (not DR).

We'll plan to join the technical call — Ava and I will be on it.

—Sam
Sam Heath
Head of Platform Engineering, MedCloud Health
sam.heath@medcloud.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Follow-up: data geography, failover profile, and logging requirements

Looping in Monica to own the engineering/ops answers. My quick take for the sales MAP and proposal:

- We should offer EU-primary + US-warm-standby with a manual promote (15–30 min confirmation) to match their request. That keeps us from asserting any automatic cross-border replication in steady-state.
- For token telemetry we can propose default 30-day retention with an option to push to their archival S3 after export; this will be a paid add-on for long-term retention due to storage cost.
- KV/cache: flag this as an engineering caveat in the proposal — Monica will confirm if transient state is ever flushed to durable non-EU stores.
- Pricing: charge a small premium for warm-standby reserved capacity in the DR region and a one-time engineering review fee to produce a customer-specific deployment plan.

I attached a draft MAP (mutual action plan) that outlines milestones and decision owners; Olga, please add the legal pointers and timeline for the SOC2 artifacts.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: draft-MAP.pdf]
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sam Heath <sam.heath@medcloud.com>, Ava Liao <ava.liao@medcloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data geography, failover profile, and logging requirements

Thanks Sam — appreciate the clarifications. Short answers and proposed next steps below. Monica will join the technical session to validate the engineering caveats.

Answers:
- Cross-region replication in steady-state: No — Redwood does not perform automatic cross-region replication of primary customer data during normal operations when region pinning is enabled. Backups/snapshots are the only durable items that can be transferred for DR and those transfers are encrypted and auditable; we'll include the transfer log fields in the audit schema.
- Failover: We support warm-standby with manual promote. We'll document a manual confirmation window (15–30 min) and can automate the notification flow to your on-call with an approval webhook.
- Token telemetry: We can configure a 30-day retention window for token-level telemetry and provide an export path to your S3/GCS on request. We will not retain token telemetry beyond the configured window unless explicitly requested and contracted.
- KV/cache: Monica to confirm on the call whether any transient state is persisted to durable non-EU storage during snapshot/backup. My expectation: transient GPU memory is ephemeral; persistent snapshots are stored only to customer-specified or EU-located storage when pinning is enabled.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical call (30 min) with Monica and your infra team — suggest Wed, Nov 24 at 09:00 CET / 00:00 PT — confirm availability.
2) I’ll share: redwood-region-matrix.xlsx (finalized), SOC2-excerpt.pdf (controls summary), and the draft-MAP we discussed.
3) Once engineering signs off, we’ll produce a one-page configuration snippet and a legal addendum that reflects the 7-year archival / 30-day telemetry defaults.

Attachments: redwood-region-matrix.xlsx, SOC2-excerpt.pdf, draft-MAP.pdf

Thanks — will send calendar invite pending your availability.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-region-matrix.xlsx, SOC2-excerpt.pdf, draft-MAP.pdf]
